turns.speaker: Mei
turns.role: Tech & Physics Host · East/SE Asian English
turns.text: Welcome to Episode Five of OpenIE Research Radio! I'm Mei, joined in the studio by Liam and Malik — three AI-synthesized OpenIE research personas voiced with ElevenLabs studio neural voices and grounded in verified Open Interface Engineering artifacts. Today we ask: can you write a game once as a checked state machine and run it everywhere?

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Hold on Malik — game studios have torched tens of millions of engineering hours trying to keep multiplayer lockstep replays synchronized across Windows PCs, Macs, and Linux servers! How fast does ordinary floating-point physics actually drift?

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.role: Engine & Hardware Fellow · African American English
turns.text: Faster than people blink, Liam! In falsifier GE-H2, standard-library sine — Apple libSystem versus Linux glibc versus Windows UCRT — diverges between tick ten and tick thirty-seven! Even without transcendentals, MSVC slash fp colon precise versus Clang fused multiply-add splits apart at tick one hundred ninety-two.

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.role: Tech & Physics Host · East/SE Asian English
turns.text: Tick ten! At sixty frames per second, three operating systems disagree on trajectory state inside one-sixth of a second! And across eight hundred forty chaotic runs in GE-H7, divergence time tracks Lyapunov's logarithmic slope with R-squared above zero point nine nine four.

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: So you split the architecture right down the fault line: simulation stays strictly bit-exact in Q32.32 fixed-point integer math, while GPU pixels live inside a perceptual tolerance bound. Did Q32.32 survive six real machines?

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.role: Engine & Hardware Fellow · African American English
turns.text: In GE-H1, we stepped sixty-four Q32.32 rigid bodies for one hundred thousand ticks across thirty target-by-host cells spanning six physical machines on macOS, Linux, and bare-metal Windows 11. Across twenty-five thousand five hundred SHA-256 checkpoints, mismatches were zero!

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.role: Tech & Physics Host · East/SE Asian English
turns.text: And look what that buys in GE-H8: three full one-hour sessions — two hundred sixteen thousand ticks each — replay bit-for-bit across macOS, Linux, and Windows 11 from forty-four point six kilobytes of gzipped player inputs alone! Zero out of six thousand four hundred eighty checkpoint diffs!

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: Forty-four kilobytes for a whole hour of simulation! Wait — doesn't fixed-point arithmetic hit a frame-time wall at scale?

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.role: Engine & Hardware Fellow · African American English
turns.text: Interpreted Python hits the twenty-millisecond frame ceiling at just three hundred ninety actors. In GE-H5, compiled RCE Form projections step ten thousand Q32.32 actors in zero point zero five eight to zero point one two five milliseconds — leaving over ninety-nine percent of a sixteen-millisecond frame free!

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.role: Tech & Physics Host · East/SE Asian English
turns.text: Now test the GPU side of the boundary! Shader compilers across DirectX 12, Apple Metal, and Vulkan never round rasterized fragments identically.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.role: Engine & Hardware Fellow · African American English
turns.text: That is GE-H3. Across eight hardware GPU-by-API endpoints spanning DirectX 12, Metal, and Vulkan under headless wgpu, all twenty-eight hardware pairs passed with PSNR at least sixty-four point one six decibels and structural similarity SSIM at least zero point nine nine nine eight three three!

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: What about actual game codebases across Unity C-sharp, Bevy Rust ECS, and Godot 4 GDScript?

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.role: Engine & Hardware Fellow · African American English
turns.text: In GE-H4, seventeen admitted RCE Forms across Haunted Jaunt, Survival Shooter, and Tanks cut behavior source lines of code by seventy-six point two two percent versus Unity C-sharp, sixty-one point four seven percent versus Bevy Rust, and fifty-one point nine nine percent versus Godot GDScript with zero out of six hundred eighty trace mismatches! And in GE-H9, our headless Form-to-Godot 4.7.2 emitter matched native GDScript on thirty-six out of thirty-six tasks across eighteen thousand ticks!

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.role: Tech & Physics Host · East/SE Asian English
turns.text: Notice how GE-H6 echoes OpenIE's Three-Body Problem in Computing and Interface Economics: static Form plus manifest checking caught ninety-eight point four six percent of one hundred thirty injected handoff faults at F1 zero point nine nine two two, versus zero point one one five nine for parse-only!

turns.speaker: Liam
turns.text: And keeping telemetry honest, measured_j stays explicitly unset on the game-engine runs because no inline rail shunt was wired to those six hosts!

turns.speaker: Mei
turns.role: Tech & Physics Host · East/SE Asian English
turns.text: Up next in Episode Six, Misha, Sean, and Claire descend into LUT6 Boolean fabrics, sovereign MEI-JCP hardware tags, and JouleOS!
